sources.title: Arch540_2026 B_testfit: PROMPTS.md and complete/ files (CLAUDE.md, brief, check.py, rules, lot, .claude/)
sources.year: 2026 (merged in r2 from five file sources)
sources.extract: PROMPTS.md: lay out buildings for maximum floor area within the rules, then draw the plan; variants add checker, skill, reviewer, hook (step 5 tries to write a developer scheme unchanged), with/without-skill comparison. complete/ holds CLAUDE.md, brief.md, check.py, layout_format.md, lot.json, rules.md, output/, work/, .claude/ (agents, hooks, skills/site-layout, settings.json). rules.md: 3 m setback; sun gap at least 0.7 x southern height where east-west extents overlap; 12 m spacing; 40 m max height with storey ranges; at least 25% unbuilt. check.py: Shapely checker, PASS/FAIL per rule, total GFA and open-space %, exit codes 0/1/2; limits: simplified sun-gap test, axis-aligned rectangles, hard-coded thresholds, GFA = footprint x storeys with no core deduction. brief.md: 2D residential test-fit; tower 18x18 m 8-12 storeys, slab 40x12 m 4-8, short 24x12 m 4-8; 3.2 m storeys; deliverables layout.json, plan.png, message naming the binding rule. Raw files read separately.

sources.title: Arch540_2026 agents_notes.html (session 4 notes, demos B, C, D)
sources.extract: B_testfit: lot 5,276 m2 (about 90 x 70 m); B1 same prompt gave 16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2; B4 reviewer APPROVE (R1-R5 PASS, both runs); B5 hook gate.py blocked a layout (R2 FAIL, gap 12.0 m, needs 26.9 m), never fired in 7 normal runs, and a hook watching the file tool missed the command line; B6 skill changed method (scheme gallery 3 of 3 vs 0 of 3), not floor area. C_design_space: 80 x 60 m Vancouver lot (49.25 N), goals GFA, winter sun (21 Dec 9:00-15:00, max 6.0 h), shape factor; C0 grid search 7,308 combos, 3,680 valid, 8 on the front; C2 no scorer 50 of 75 valid vs scorer 61 of 75; C3 one run imported the scoring functions so evaluations were never counted; C5 six helpers, main context near 50k tokens; one-run test note gives rows 82, north-high-south-low 80, terraced 18 (sum 180, three of six helpers; others not given), a 300-evaluation cap enforced by the scoring script, a prompt asking about 40 each (about 240), and 329 evaluations in total at step 5, none reconciled; C6 impossible target stopped after 5 (no hook) or 7 (hook) evaluations. D_team: 100 x 70 m block, FSR 2.8, 220-280 homes; hidden contradiction (CEO wants 250+ homes, FSR allows about 239) caught by the constraints helper in 3 of 3 runs; three runs, three schemes (237, 222, 226 homes); D3 without the helper a designer estimated about 255 homes, tool measured 223; round 1 4 of 12 schemes failed (3 play-area sun, 1 park shadow), round 2 12 of 12 passed, with no run count stated: the notes describe all eight schemes of one run (two rounds of four), so 12 is inferred as totals across 3 runs. Lessons: checks in code hold where requests do not; a guard covers only the path it watches; measure rather than estimate; run several times.

case_studies.tool: GenEnv/Arch540_2026 demo D_team (mixed-use block with a hidden FSR contradiction)
case_studies.what_it_does: Course demo of about 10 agents on a 100 x 70 m corner block (streets south and east, park north; FSR 2.8, 220-280 homes, daycare, no new park shadow 10:00-14:00 at equinox): an orchestrator, a constraints helper that turns the brief into a checklist and flags contradictions before design, four parallel designers, an analyst that reports numbers only, and a reviewer that sees only the checklist and metrics; blackboard files have one owner each, hooks block edits to tools and failing final schemes.
case_studies.how_used: Copy complete/ (or steps/no_constraints/), run claude, paste the prompt; a run takes 30-60 min and can use up a Pro plan's 5-hour allowance (S56).
case_studies.strengths: Constraints helper caught the contradiction (CEO wants 250+ homes, FSR allows about 239) in 3 of 3 runs, before design, with a calculation; without it a designer estimated about 255 homes and the tool measured 223 (D3). Same brief gave three different recommendations (237, 222, 226 homes). Totals across 3 runs (inferred): round 1, 4 of 12 schemes failed a hard rule; round 2, 12 of 12 passed (the notes' eight schemes describe one run). Template for a PROG constraints reader checking 9.0 FSR non-residential against height and plate assumptions (S09).
case_studies.stops_at: Housing-scale block with FSR 2.8, not 9.0 non-residential; different recommendations per run mean a single run cannot be trusted; expensive in plan allowance; no licence stated.
case_studies.license_cost: Free to clone; no licence declared; heavy plan allowance use.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: AI: a brief-to-checklist reader that flags contradictions before design (its answers varied run to run). CODE: limits.json (18 agent calls, 8 designer calls, 2 rounds) and the analyst's measured numbers. PEOPLE: the reviewer confirms.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: PEOPLE: which contradiction to resolve and how (relax a target, argue a breach); whether the scheme suits the site's culture and public realm. AI: a single LLM run cannot be trusted.
case_studies.workflow_step: As-is steps 0, 3 (brief reading and programme/FSR checking)
case_studies.access_for_vtc_team: FREE to clone; needs Python 3 and a Claude plan (30-60 min runs, may exhaust a Pro 5-hour allowance). Usable before 30 Nov: yes as a pattern, at a cost in allowance; reuse terms unresolved. Sources: S02, S56.

case_studies.tool: SimScale (added in r1; wind route candidate)
case_studies.what_it_does: Cloud engineering simulation (CFD, structural, thermal) with AEC listed as an industry and Wind and Built Environment as an application; Community plan free; academic plans exist (S68).
case_studies.how_used: Upload geometry, set up a simulation in the browser, run in the cloud (setup depth not opened).
case_studies.strengths: Free Community plan with 10 simulations and up to 2,000 core hours; Free Academic Plan with 1,000 core hours and private projects (PWC excluded); a real CFD route if a surrogate is not trusted.
case_studies.stops_at: After the Community limit only qualitative output; pedestrian wind comfort is a Specialized add-on on Professional and Enterprise only, and PWC is excluded from the Free Academic Plan; Community projects are implied public (anonymity risk); no stated validity range for 244-305 m towers; setup skill needed.
case_studies.license_cost: Community free (no private projects); Free Academic Plan (1,000 core hours, private projects; thesis students 12 months); Academic Sponsorship Plan for student design-competition teams by application (terms unknown); Professional on request (S58, S68).
case_studies.ai_opportunity: AI: could script case set-up via API (not verified) and tabulate results across massing options; CODE: the solver itself.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: PEOPLE: CFD boundary conditions, mesh quality and comfort criteria need expert judgement.
case_studies.access_for_vtc_team: Community (public projects implied) or Academic Sponsorship Plan by application (terms and turnaround unknown; academic-program@simscale.com). Free Academic Plan targets thesis students. Usable before 30 Nov: yes for basic CFD on Community; tower adequacy unknown; public projects can expose the scheme before judging. Sources: S58, S68.

case_studies.tool: EC3 and tallyLCA (Building Transparency; added in r1)
case_studies.what_it_does: EC3 is a free, open-access tool and EPD database for estimating upfront embodied carbon and setting baselines; tallyLCA is a whole-building life cycle assessment tool for architects.
case_studies.how_used: Sign up, search and compare product EPDs, estimate embodied carbon of a project (workflow not opened).
case_studies.strengths: Free and open-access EC3; a sourced route to embodied-carbon numbers instead of unsourced rules of thumb.
case_studies.stops_at: Early-stage massing use not described; terms of use and limits not read; tallyLCA availability and cost not stated; not a Vancouver or VTC benchmark.
case_studies.license_cost: EC3 free (vendor page); tallyLCA not stated.
case_studies.ai_opportunity: AI: map a programme and structure assumption to EPD queries and tabulate options; CODE: the EPD database look-ups.
case_studies.ai_wont_improve: PEOPLE: structural system and material choice; which carbon benchmark applies in Vancouver.
case_studies.access_for_vtc_team: FREE (EC3, sign-up form; terms unread). Usable before 30 Nov: probably yes; tallyLCA unknown. Sources: S59.

as_is_workflow.step: 0. Register, plan the 40 days, read the brief
as_is_workflow.who: All 2-4 members; one person owns the checklist and the calendar
as_is_workflow.software: PDF reader, shared drive, chat, spreadsheet or whiteboard, calendar; Buildner account
as_is_workflow.input: VTC brief PDF and site plans and 3D model (linked on the competition page; not opened by this packet); policy documents the City page and brief name: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) and Higher Buildings Policy Review (S71), Public Views Guidelines 2024 for views (S69, second-hand).
as_is_workflow.output: Requirements checklist: deliverables, 9.0 FSR non-residential minimum, jury weights 40/30/20/10, deadlines, fee, and the Student Award and Sustainability Award (CAD 1,000 each, S01); role split; back-plan. Illustrative back-plan (team assumption): massing frozen about 9 Nov; studies 16 Nov; plans and sections 21 Nov; board drafts 25 Nov; upload dry-run 28 Nov.
as_is_workflow.pain_points: As of 21 Oct 2026: registration closes in 8 days (29 Oct), Q&A in 13 (3 Nov, no later questions), course working core in 23 (13 Nov), submission in 40 (30 Nov 23:59 London = 15:59 Pacific, derived). FSR basis, view-cone applicability and site georeference must be asked by 3 Nov. Fee: student EUR 120, others EUR 140, plus 4.5% VAT, one payment or 3 monthly instalments (S01). City pages returned 403 to scripts; a person opens them. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Reading notes to everyone else; usually a chat message or a doc nobody updates
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Day counts, the London-to-Pacific conversion and 11,468 m2 x 9.0 FSR are plain arithmetic (derived from S01 dimensions; FSR basis unconfirmed).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can draft a deadline and contradiction checklist from the brief; demo D's constraints helper caught a hidden contradiction in 3 of 3 runs, yet three runs gave three different schemes, so answers vary and need checking (S09).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Interpreting City in Nature and reconciliation, which guideline to breach, whether to enter and pay, roles and the back-plan (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.step: 0b. Cultural, geographic and precedent research and narrative
as_is_workflow.who: All members read; 1-2 lead the narrative; no tool substitutes for engagement
as_is_workflow.software: Library and web sources, reading notes, shared document, image collection
as_is_workflow.input: Brief statement that the site is on the unceded territories of the Musqueam, Squamish and Tsleil-Waututh Nations; City UNDRIP Strategy (adopted 25 Oct 2022 with the three Nations, 79 calls to action, Action Plan 2024-2028; S72, 403, second-hand); the Nations' own sites (S73, homepages opened); precedents. Sources the team reads, not data the tool interprets.
as_is_workflow.output: Written cultural and environmental narrative with cited sources; precedent list; design principles that feed massing, ground level and boards
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Carries 30% of jury weight yet is easily compressed into a paragraph at the end (team assumption); risk of generic or placeless motifs, which the brief warns against; the Nations' homepages state no engagement protocols (S73), so the team contacts them directly; sources must be cited without identifying the team on boards. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Narrative to board designers late; principles often do not reach massing or ground-level decisions
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Citation bookkeeping only: store each source's URL, retrieval date and quote, and flag uncited claims (team assumption); code does not judge cultural content.
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: May help retrieve and summarise published documents with the citation attached, checked against the source; no sourced evidence of LLM accuracy for this task (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Interpreting Indigenous perspectives, deciding what to represent and how, and any contact with the Nations stay human-only; the team reads the Nations' and City's own documents (S72, S73).

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino (or SketchUp), imported OBJ/IFC/3DM, maybe Speckle; City of Vancouver open data for context
as_is_workflow.input: Provided site plan and 3D model; context towers, approved future towers; north arrow rotated from the street grid; City open data (building footprints 1999/2009/2015, zoning districts, building lines found in a title search; no 3D massing dataset appeared; licences not checked)
as_is_workflow.output: Georeferenced site and context model, true-north vector, block area (79.2 x 144.8 m = 11,468 m2)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Orientation error is the costly one: the plan's north arrow is rotated from the street grid, so a wrong angle corrupts every later sun and shadow result. Units come in ft and m (260 x 475 ft = 79.2 x 144.8 m). Imports lose layers or tags (team assumption). Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Model file passed by drive or email; versions drift; no programme tags yet; Speckle Explore keeps only 30 days of versions
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Unit conversion (260 x 475 ft = 79.2 x 144.8 m), block area 11,468 m2, orientation and import checks are deterministic (derived from S01).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can write import or conversion scripts (Claude Code writes Python and Grasshopper code, team assumption); it cannot tell which context matters.
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Which context buildings matter, and whether true north matches the provided plan (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.who: One designer with the modeller; checked by the whole team
as_is_workflow.software: Rhino with imported view-cone polygons (City GeoJSON export), sketching, photo montage
as_is_workflow.input: City open-data View cones (24 polygons, four QE Park views 3.2.1-3.2.4; Open Government Licence - Vancouver; modified 19 Oct 2026; S54); Public Views Guidelines (Council-approved 10 July 2024; replaced the 1989 VPG; PDF 403, second-hand, S69); Higher Buildings Policy 1997 (403, S62); the City says protected views are outside the review (S71); brief's skyline view from Queen Elizabeth Park.
as_is_workflow.output: Permissible-height envelope per view cone (once heights are read from the guidelines), skyline sketch, list of any intended breach with justification
as_is_workflow.pain_points: UNVERIFIED: the dataset says height is limited inside these views but has no height field and the PDFs could not be opened, so heights and whether the hypothetical block lies in a cone are unknown. The 24 records are consistent with 38 views minus 14 removed in 2024 (inference). Checked late, a 244-305 m massing may need rework (team assumption). Justified breaches may be rewarded (earlier-round read; brief not opened).
as_is_workflow.handover: Envelope from views person to massing designers; skyline view to rendering step 7
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Loading the 24 view-cone polygons (S54) and clipping a massing against them is deterministic once a person has read the height rule from the Public Views Guidelines (rule UNVERIFIED, S69).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM could quote the height clause once a person opens the PDF; the quote must be checked against the PDF (team assumption, no sourced accuracy).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Reading the guidelines, choosing whether to breach, and the skyline composition (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino/Grasshopper, SketchUp, sketch paper; sometimes Forma (free for students, vendor statement) or TestFit if licensed
as_is_workflow.input: Site model, view envelope, brief heights (244-305 m), required mix, hand sketches
as_is_workflow.output: 2-5 massing models; each tagged by use if time allows (becomes Layer 0)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Options compared by eye; every change means recomputing areas by hand; option count limited by modelling time. Time share unmeasured, believed largest (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Models to the spreadsheet person and to the environmental analyst, usually as screenshots or a copied file
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Generating variants and measuring them: demo C scorer, front file and spending cap in code (7,308 combinations, 3,680 valid, 8 on the front; S09).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can propose families and steer rounds; with a scorer 61 of 75 designs were valid vs 50 of 75 guessing, and demo B's same prompt gave 16,272 / 13,968 / 15,552 m2, so runs vary (S09).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Form, skyline silhouette, expression, the public-uses-through-the-tower idea and which goals count (team judgment).
tools_from_case_studies: GenEnv/Arch540_2026 demo C_design_space (Vancouver winter-sun trade-off front)

as_is_workflow.who: One person (often the least modelling-heavy member)
as_is_workflow.input: Floor areas read off the models; use mix; efficiency and core assumptions
as_is_workflow.output: GFA by use, non-residential FSR (brief minimum 9.0), area schedule for the boards
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Manual copy from model to sheet drifts after each massing change. Derived check, assuming the full block as FSR basis (unconfirmed): 11,468 m2 x 9.0 = about 103,200 m2 non-residential. Derived relationship (editable placeholders, not sourced): office floors N = 103,200 / plate; 1,500 m2 gives about 69 floors, 2,000 about 52, 2,500 about 41; at an assumed 4.0 m floor-to-floor that is about 276, 208 and 165 m, so a small plate could use most of a 244-305 m height unless podium floors carry area.
as_is_workflow.handover: Spreadsheet numbers to the board designer; numbers on boards later disagree with the model
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Area take-off, FSR arithmetic, the floors-versus-height calculation and model-to-sheet consistency checks are deterministic (derived from S01; plates are placeholders).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM constraints reader can flag contradictions before design (demo D: 3 of 3 runs on an FSR 2.8 brief) and draft the mix table, but outputs vary run to run (S09).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Mix, efficiencies, what counts as high-employment use, and the FSR basis (ask in the Q&A by 3 Nov) (team judgment).
tools_from_case_studies: GenEnv/Arch540_2026 demo D_team (mixed-use block with a hidden FSR contradiction)

as_is_workflow.software: SketchUp shadows or Rhino sun, Ladybug/Grasshopper, optionally Forma (vendor-stated sun and wind), Infrared.city, SimScale, Eddy3D (wind candidate); CFD rarely

as_is_workflow.output: Shadow images, sun-hour maps, a qualitative or surrogate wind note
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Run once on the final option rather than to compare options; results are pictures without a pass/fail criterion or source; wind is the study most likely to be skipped (team assumption); tool access (Rhino USD 195 student; Infrared tokens expire 42 days after sign-up, about 2 Dec if activated 21 Oct; run wind by mid-November, team assumption); cloud tools may expose the scheme (public-project risk).
as_is_workflow.handover: Images to boards; findings rarely feed back into massing
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Sun hours, shadow areas and surrogate wind maps come from engines (Ladybug, Forma sun study, Infrared); vendor thresholds are not exposed (S64, S31).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can script batch runs and tabulate results per option; it cannot check whether a surrogate is valid for 244-305 m (UNVERIFIED, S30).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Choosing the criterion, day or season, and whether a result is acceptable (team judgment).
tools_from_case_studies: GenEnv/Arch540_2026 demo C_design_space (Vancouver winter-sun trade-off front)

as_is_workflow.who: The environment person plus one designer
as_is_workflow.software: Ladybug/Honeybee, spreadsheet, EC3 (free), Forma embodied-carbon analysis (vendor-stated), possibly a Pollination trial; cove analysis.tool is not available to students
as_is_workflow.input: Massing, envelope assumptions (glazing ratio, systems), weather file, material quantities
as_is_workflow.output: Sustainability diagram or short study for the boards (the brief lists sustainability studies among recommended deliverables, r1 read); embodied-carbon estimate
as_is_workflow.pain_points: The Sustainability Award (CAD 1,000, S01) bears on whether this step deserves time. Benchmarks and efficiency targets are usually unsourced; energy models need envelope and systems assumptions students invent (team assumption); often reduced to a diagram late. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Numbers and diagrams to boards; rarely fed back into facade or massing
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Weather processing, solar radiation, simple energy runs and EPD look-ups (EC3) are deterministic once inputs are chosen (S20, S59).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can map a programme and structure assumption to EPD queries and tabulate options (team assumption); no sourced accuracy.
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Strategy, targets, material and structure choice, and trade-offs against daylight and cost (team judgment).
tools_from_case_studies: EC3 and tallyLCA (Building Transparency; added in r1)

as_is_workflow.who: Designer; no engineer on most student teams
as_is_workflow.software: Hand sketches, Illustrator or CAD, rules of thumb
as_is_workflow.input: Massing, height, programme, lift and stair rules of thumb
as_is_workflow.output: Structural strategy diagram, core layout, typical plan cores
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Core and structure sizes are rule-of-thumb and unsourced; core area in the spreadsheet and in plans disagree; structure rarely tested against massing changes (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.handover: Core areas back to the spreadsheet by hand
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Preliminary sizing from stated rules, only if the rules are sourced (team assumption; none sourced here).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can look up code clauses, but UpCodes jurisdiction coverage is unconfirmed (S28); no sourced accuracy.
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: The structural concept and its architectural expression (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.step: 6. Ground level, transit, servicing and public realm
as_is_workflow.input: Site edges (arterial, retail high street, lanes, mid-block connections), below-grade secondary transit entrance requirement, loading and parking needs
as_is_workflow.output: Ground-floor plan, site plan, below-grade connection, servicing diagram
as_is_workflow.pain_points: This is where human-scale experience (40% of jury weight) is decided yet it is often drawn last (team assumption); loading, parking and transit link are coordinated by eye.
as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Clearances, loading counts and path lengths can be checked by script (team assumption; no tool sourced).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: No sourced AI role; an LLM could write the path-length scripts (team assumption).

as_is_workflow.software: Rhino/CAD (Make2D or equivalent), Illustrator or AutoCAD, Revit or Archicad if used
as_is_workflow.input: Frozen massing, programme, cores and structure, ground-level design
as_is_workflow.output: Site plan, ground floor plan, typical lower, mid and upper plans, at least two sections (brief's recommended deliverables)
as_is_workflow.pain_points: Plans are redrawn after every massing or core change; cut positions chosen late; core and area labels disagree with the spreadsheet (team assumption); line weights and scale inconsistent across boards. Time share unmeasured.
as_is_workflow.handover: Drawings to board designers as PDFs or Illustrator files, often in mixed formats

as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: No sourced AI role; an LLM could script area labelling (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Which cuts to show, drawing conventions and spatial quality (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.software: Enscape, Twinmotion, Lumion, V-Ray or similar; Photoshop; possibly AI image tools
as_is_workflow.input: Final model, camera positions (skyline from Queen Elizabeth Park, mid-city, at least four ground-level perspectives)

as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Batch rendering and camera setup from coordinates are deterministic (team assumption).

as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Composition, story and drawing choices (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.software: Word processor or shared document; policy PDFs opened by hand
as_is_workflow.input: Higher Buildings Policy (1997) and the Higher Buildings Policy Review (S71); Public Views Guidelines (2024) and the dataset's 24 views (S69, S54); the scheme's actual heights, FSR and view-cone position; the brief's statement that its documents are academic, not legal (earlier-round read, brief not opened)
as_is_workflow.output: Written policy reflection for the boards, listing where the scheme follows, tests or breaches guidelines, with justification

as_is_workflow.decided_by_code: Listing which numeric thresholds the scheme exceeds, once rules are entered with their source (team assumption).
as_is_workflow.assisted_by_ai: An LLM can retrieve and summarise clauses with a citation once a person has opened the 403 PDFs (S62, S69); no sourced accuracy.
as_is_workflow.decided_by_people: Which guideline to breach and why (team judgment).

as_is_workflow.output: Uploaded entry before 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time (15:59 Pacific, derived)

notes:
Method: every claim is from a page opened on 21 Oct 2026 (rounds 0, r1, r2) unless labelled UNVERIFIED, second-hand or team assumption. Prices are as shown that day in the vendor's currency and may change. Page text came through a summarising fetch tool. r2: the reviser's web-search budget was exhausted again, so facts known only from the r2 critic's search pass (Autodesk education page, Public Views Guidelines, Council 10 July 2024 papers, vancouver.ca review page, UNDRIP Strategy, Food4Rhino Eddy3D date) are labelled second-hand with opened:false. Where a primary page was reachable it was re-read (Forma blog, Snaptrude, SimScale academic, Rhino, Infrared, Buildner, Shape Your City, Nations' sites, Eddy3D).

Key facts for the team (21 Oct 2026): registration closes 29 Oct, Q&A 3 Nov, submission 30 Nov 23:59 London (40 days); teams up to 4; fee student EUR 120, others EUR 140, plus 4.5% VAT; prizes CAD 15,000 including Student and Sustainability Awards of CAD 1,000. What a student team can get before 30 Nov: Autodesk Forma free (vendor statement; eligibility to confirm logged in); Snaptrude Student Plan free (educational use only; prize-competition question open); Rhino USD 195 student, or a 30-user lab licence at USD 975 if UBC buys; Ladybug Tools free; Speckle Explore plus an academic workspace (terms unknown); Giraffe free (vendor statement, Vancouver data unverified); Infrared Free 900 tokens (42 days); Finch free single-user tier (no education offer found); SimScale Community (projects implied public) or Academic Sponsorship by application; EC3 free; ShapeDiver 14-day trial or academic; Eddy3D wind candidate (licence unverified). Not available to students: cove analysis.tool. Unknown: TestFit class terms, Hypar, Archistar, UpCodes.

Design lessons for the tool: (1) no commercial tool opened exposes sourced thresholds (Forma's criteria are unverified), so they are benchmarks, not dependencies; (2) open, scriptable options are Ladybug Tools (AGPL-3.0 for ladybug, ladybug-grasshopper, honeybee-radiance; GPL-3.0+ for Butterfly), Speckle (Apache-2.0) and Hypar Elements/HyparSpace (MIT); the platform licence and deployment boundary go to the DATA packet because AGPL section 13 attaches to modified versions offered over a network; (3) the course demos give three module patterns: B (checker script, hook, reviewer), C (scorer, front file, rounds, cap in code, per-family helpers) and D (constraints reader that flags contradictions before design, analyst that reports only measured numbers); each shows a guard covers only the path it watches; (4) code, AI and people are now separated per step: code results are measurements, LLM helpers vary run to run (demo D), and people decide criteria, interpretation of City in Nature and reconciliation, which guideline to breach, and any engagement with the Nations; (5) protected views now point to the Public Views Guidelines (2024), whose heights a person must read from the PDF (403); the City dataset's 24 polygons are the verified starting point; (6) cloud tools may expose the entry before anonymous judging.

As-is evidence: all time shares and pain points remain team assumptions (interview n=0). Before 13 Nov run at least two 15-minute interviews (VTC-registered SALA teams or past tall-building competition entrants); ask per step: hours spent, tool, who, what was redone, what was skipped, where the handover broke; record answers with dates and relabel confirmed steps interview n=2. Until then the step ranking must not drive module priority.
